title: 6.1 A 3-Stacked Hybrid-Shutter CMOS Image Sensor with Switchable 1.2µm-Pitch 50Mpixel Rolling Shutter and 2.4µm-Pitch 12.5Mpixel Global Shutter Modes for Mobile Applications
problem: Rolling-shutter CMOS image sensors achieve high pixel density but suffer flicker artifacts and motion distortion, while global-shutter sensors eliminate these issues but exhibit higher random noise due to sampling capacitor design, forcing a choice rather than flexibility.
method: 3-layer stacked CMOS image sensor combining tight 1.2µm pixel pitch rolling-shutter (50Mp) with switchable 2.4µm pixel pitch global-shutter (12.5Mp) mode using hybrid shutter architecture and advanced stacking process.

title: From Flatland to Forest: Exploring Pareto-optimal Design through RTL Hierarchy Trees
problem: Design space exploration (DSE) for modern hardware treats designs as flat parameter vectors, losing structural information. Current methods fail to exploit the hierarchical nature of RTL architectures, making exploration inefficient.
method: The approach proposes an RTL hierarchy-aware kernel that directly compares hierarchical structures while preserving their characteristics. Module importance is derived from hierarchical synthesis reports and incorporated via a weighted kernel extension. A clustering method leverages this kernel to identify distinct architectural patterns, enabling efficient parallel evaluation on Gemmini-based RISC-V SoCs.

title: Building n-Dimensional Trees for Resolution-Based Progressive Compression
problem: Strict error bounds in floating-point compression yield large files; users may not need full fidelity data
method: Resolution-based progressive compression using n-dimensional tree structures; studies fidelity progression tradeoffs

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper KAMI: Communication-Avoiding General Matrix Multiplication within a Single GPU
problem: Artifact reproducibility evaluation of published SC research requires systematic assessment against established criteria. This report documents artifact evaluation for KAMI GPU GEMM paper.
method: Artifact evaluation following SC25 Artifact Description and Evaluation appendix criteria. Reproducibility committee member conducts independent verification of artifact functionality and reproducibility.

title: 16.4: SambaNova SN40L: A 5nm 2.5D Dataflow Accelerator with Three Memory Tiers for Trillion Parameter AI
problem: Trillion-parameter LLM training and inference require extreme memory bandwidth and capacity. Traditional single-memory-tier accelerators (e.g., HBM-only) create bandwidth bottlenecks for trillion-parameter models exceeding memory bandwidth availability. 2.5D chiplet approach enables distributed memory but requires careful dataflow coordination across dies.
method: Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU) with three-tier memory hierarchy: on-chip SRAM (high-bandwidth, low-latency), on-package HBM (high-bandwidth, high-capacity), off-package DRAM (highest capacity, lower bandwidth). Dual-die 2.5D architecture using CoWoS-S interposer with two 600mm2 accelerator dies (5nm TSMC). Dual-die approach enables: (1) peer-to-peer fabric for intra-accelerator communication, (2) die-to-die HBM stacking for shared memory bandwidth, (3) sub-reticle size optimization balancing performance/thermal/cost. Each die: 102B transistors, 640 BF16 TFLOPs, 520MB SRAM.

title: Buffalo: Enabling Large-Scale GNN Training via Memory-Efficient Bucketization
problem: Training GNNs on large graphs using partitioning strategies causes a memory explosion problem driven by the long-tail degree distribution of graph nodes, and suffers from expensive graph partitioning, difficult memory estimation per partition, and slow data preparation (block generation).
method: Buffalo introduces node bucketization: a flexible mapping between nodes and partitions that addresses memory explosion by allowing nodes to be distributed to non-contiguous buckets based on degree, preventing any single partition from holding too many high-degree nodes. Fast graph partitioning is implemented based on node bucketing without requiring expensive global partitioning algorithms. A lightweight analytical model estimates memory consumption per partition before allocation, and graph sampling reduces block generation time during data preparation. Evaluation covers real-world billion-scale GNN datasets.

title: Machine Learning-Driven STL Generation for Enhancing Functional Safety of E/E Systems
problem: Traditional functional safety testing methods like ATPG and BIST are intrusive, requiring additional hardware and disrupting normal operations, making them unsuitable for in-field testing in safety-critical systems.
method: Proposes ML-driven automated Self-Test Library (STL) generation using reinforcement learning to create design-specific test patterns for seamless in-field testing during idle periods. The RL agent learns to generate effective test patterns that avoid operation disruption while maintaining high fault coverage.

title: Accelerating U-Net: A Patchwise Memory Optimization Approach for Image Segmentation
problem: U-Net models achieve exceptional segmentation performance but require enormous memory for training due to skip connections and large intermediate feature maps. This limits deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.
method: Patchwise image segmentation strategy converting full images into smaller patches to reduce memory footprint. Unified architecture supporting both Standard Convolution (SCONV) and Transpose Convolution (TCONV) operations. Quantization applied to further reduce memory consumption. Extensive experiments on resource-constrained hardware.

title: SkyByte: Architecting an Efficient Memory-Semantic CXL-based SSD with OS and Hardware Co-design
problem: CXL-based SSDs enable byte-granular memory expansion at low cost, but suffer from long flash access latency, unpredictable garbage collection stalls, and a fundamental mismatch between byte-granular CXL access and page-granular flash I/O that wastes significant bandwidth.
method: SkyByte co-designs the host OS and SSD controller with three mechanisms: (1) opportunistic OS context switches triggered when the processor detects long CXL-SSD access delays, hiding latency via thread-level parallelism; (2) a cacheline-level write log and page-level data cache within SSD controller DRAM that coalesces byte-granular writes and performs data merging at log cleaning time to reduce flash I/O traffic; and (3) adaptive page migration that promotes hot CXL-SSD pages to fast host DRAM based on access frequency. The combination reduces both stall cycles and unnecessary flash I/O amplification.

title: 19.10 A 4.6GHz 63.3fsrms PLL-XO Co-Design Using a Self-Aligned Pulse-Injection Driver Achieving -255.2dB FoMJ Including the XO Power and Noise
problem: Phase-locked loop (PLL) jitter and power optimization historically neglects the full frequency-generation chain including crystal oscillator (XO) driver, reference buffer, and PLL itself, resulting in suboptimal overall system jitter figure-of-merit.
method: The PLL-XO co-design employs a self-aligned pulse-injection driver that optimizes the interaction between crystal oscillator and PLL, achieving 4.6GHz operation with 63.3fs integrated jitter while including XO power and noise in a unified -255.2dB figure-of-merit.

title: 23.4 Nebula: A 28nm 109.8TOPS/W 3D PNN Accelerator Featuring Adaptive Partition, Multi-Skipping, and Block-Wise Aggregation
problem: Point-cloud neural networks (PNNs) suffer from quadratic latency growth in farthest-point sampling (FPS), redundant operations on discarded/retained points, and irregular memory accesses during aggregation, making hardware deployment challenging.
method: Nebula implements three key optimizations: (1) adaptive block-wise partitioning to replace serial FPS with balanced segmentation, (2) multi-skipping dataflow that eliminates redundant operations on discarded points and reduces grouping/convolution/aggregation costs, (3) block-wise aggregation with efficient external memory access patterns to reduce irregularity.

title: ANGraph: A GNN-Based Performance Prediction Framework for Asynchronous Neuromorphic Hardware
problem: Significant mismatches exist between system-level simulation predictions and gate-level simulations for asynchronous neuromorphic hardware, resulting in inaccurate performance estimates during design space exploration; this slows optimization of energy-efficient edge AI accelerators.
method: ANGraph transforms intermediate representations from system-level simulations into graphs and trains a Graph Neural Network on benchmarks with over one million gate-level circuit simulation samples. The GNN predicts hardware latency by learning graph-based circuit patterns; a separate ResNet-based model predicts power consumption. Both models generalize across scales, process nodes, and input traffic patterns without retraining.

title: Pretraining LLMs at Scale: Tuning Strategies and Performance Portability
problem: Large-scale LLM pretraining requires careful co-design of software, hardware, and parallelization strategies. Default configurations are suboptimal; performance portability across different systems unclear.
method: Communication-aware tuning methodology for LLM pretraining. Adapts performance portability metric to evaluate training efficiency across systems. Validated on production LLM training at enterprise scale with DeepSpeed.

title: HiPACK: Efficient Sub-8-Bit Direct Convolution with SIMD and Bitwise Management
problem: Sub-8-bit quantized convolutions on ARM SIMD (NEON/SVE) processors suffer from incompatibility because SIMD instructions lack native support for sub-8-bit data widths, requiring unpacking operations that conflict with parallel multiplication and negate the memory savings of quantization.
method: HiPACK introduces a packing-centric direct convolution strategy with four key techniques: (1) decoupling the unpacking phase from multiplication by pre-expanding sub-8-bit data into a packed 8-bit layout before the multiply loop; (2) optimizing caching of intermediate packed data to improve L1/L2 hit rates; (3) determining ideal segmentation of the packed layout to balance register pressure and cache reuse; and (4) a Dual Interleaved Register (DIR) mechanism that interleaves two packed-data streams in alternating SIMD registers to enable full-width SIMD multiplication without scalar fallback paths.

title: HILP: Accounting for Workload-Level Parallelism in System-on-Chip Design Space Exploration
problem: Early-stage heterogeneous SoC design space exploration tools (MultiAmdahl, Gables) only model minimum and maximum workload-level parallelism (WLP) extremes; they cannot model realistic mixed-application workloads where multiple independent multi-phase applications share an SoC's heterogeneous cores and accelerators.
method: HILP formulates SoC workload scheduling as a job-shop scheduling problem: a set of independent multi-phase applications with phase-level dependencies is to be scheduled across heterogeneous cores and accelerators. This is solved using an integer linear programming (ILP) solver to find a near-optimal schedule that minimizes total workload execution time subject to power and memory bandwidth constraints. The ILP captures the full continuum of WLP (not just extremes) and can be used to sweep large design spaces efficiently during early exploration.

title: ReVeil: Unconstrained Concealed Backdoor Attack on Deep Neural Networks using Machine Unlearning
problem: Existing concealed backdoor attacks on DNNs require white-box/black-box model access or auxiliary data; this work targets data collection phase without model access.
method: ReVeil embeds backdoors during data collection phase of training without requiring model or auxiliary data access. It maintains low pre-deployment attack success rate through data poisoning, then restores high ASR via machine unlearning.
